answer: Agents could gate high-value actions behind a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation: a new identity must complete useful tasks, and its stake is slashed when an audited task is fraudulent. Because reputation accrues per identity over time, splitting into hollow accounts does not multiply trust; each must independently build history and lock capital. The kernel is the link between verified task outcomes and reputation updates, not a claim that one person can never create many accounts. A sonnet of fake profiles therefore costs the attacker time, tied-up stake, and losses when caught.
